semgrep.triage: One audit warning in the existing MIME boundary RegExp. Boundary metacharacters are escaped into a literal and body bytes are bounded; no attacker-controlled regex syntax is inserted. This warning is recorded rather than counted as a newly fixed vulnerability. One pre-existing TS inline import type is unsupported by the scanner parser; TypeScript checking and transpiled JS scan passed.

android-ui-observation.automationNote: Initial Calendar selector used the iOS tab label; retried with observed Android label without repeating completion.

notes: An immediate snapshot at the end of navigation preceded the updated frame. A subsequent capture had a different foreground application. Neither was counted as Calendar success. LiFlow was activated explicitly and the Calendar tree and screen were verified in step250.
No other foreground application was operated.

verificationNotes: The first full run exposed4 compatibility failures; transport test doubles and the waste-header access bound were corrected. A reservation test gate was moved from runAsync to getAllAsync because the new SQL uses INSERT RETURNING; transaction-cancellation assertions remain unchanged. The final whole suite passed.

The normal emulator ports were occupied and system Java was too old. The successful Cloud run used a separate loopback configuration and the existing Android Studio JBR25; no other emulator was stopped.

Native probes use a separate Android application and disposable SQLite database, both removed after the9 checks. Normal applications were updated in place using existing signatures and existing native Release binaries with newly compiled Hermes JS.

Native screen checks verify the observed completion, undo, and navigation state. They do not establish every-frame latency, new long-duration natural background execution, all Google live account paths, paid AI or store purchases.
Weather service changes are source/test verified. No production backend deployment was performed in this audit.
This is development verification, not an independent third-party security audit.
